1.explanation:
All of these files live under the `docs/reveal` tree, which contains the built-in examples and tests for the Quarto revealjs format.  

• index.qmd shows the basic YAML front-matter for revealjs and default width/height settings.  
• output-location.qmd illustrates how the reveal slides are laid out in the output directory.  
• stretch.qmd demonstrates the use of width/height stretching options, closely related to percent-based sizing.  
• The mini examples (absolute.qmd, auto-animate.qmd, zoom.qmd) exercise specific revealjs features (absolute positioning, auto-animate, zoom) that overlap with the user’s use of `auto-animate` and help verify whether percent-based dimensions break those features.  

Inspecting these documents will show how Quarto’s revealjs templates expect numeric dimensions (unquoted) and reveal where percent strings are not being quoted or passed through correctly in the generated HTML, leading to the blank screen.
1.bug_scenario: When you author a Quarto revealjs presentation and set the slide `width` and `height` in percent (e.g. width: "100%", height: "100%") inside the YAML front-matter, the rendered presentation shows a blank/black screen instead of your slides. If you instead specify explicit pixel values (e.g. width: 1600, height: 900), the slides render correctly. In the example the user also uses an `auto-animate` attribute on a slide heading, but nothing is displayed when percent dimensions are used.
